content.text: I couldn't see the code for the password-change path, so these locations are inferred from the call graph and the bug report. I haven't confirmed them against the source.

candidates.explanation: This is probably where the password-change branch ends the user's other sessions. The call likely passes the wrong value as the session to keep. For example, it may use the user id, or `currentUser.id`, instead of the current session id from the JWT payload (`userJwtPayload.sessionId`). It may also drop the exclusion entirely or exclude the wrong field. The current session would then be deleted, so the next refresh-token call returns 401. An unrelated older session would be the one that survives. The line numbers are an estimate from the L426 start of `update`. I didn't see this code.

If the call site is correct, the fault may be in the repository delete. The exclusion filter could be inverted or wrong, for example `id: Not(...)` built from the wrong field or a type mismatch. The document repository has the same risk. It would then delete the excluded session and keep others. The line numbers are an estimate. I didn't see this code.

fix.description: In AuthService.update, when the password changes, call sessionService.deleteByUserIdWithExclude({ userId: currentUser.id, excludeId: userJwtPayload.sessionId }). Pass the current session id from the JWT payload, converted to the same type the repository compares against. Also check that the repository delete uses a 'not equal to excludeId' filter on the session id and the user's id.

For example, it may use the user id, or `currentUser.id`, instead of the current session id from the JWT payload (`userJwtPayload.sessionId`). It may also drop the exclusion entirely or exclude the wrong field. The current session would then be deleted, so the next refresh-token call returns 401. fix.description: In AuthService.update, when the password changes, call sessionService.deleteByUserIdWithExclude({ userId: currentUser.id, excludeId: userJwtPayload.sessionId }). Pass the current session id from the JWT payload, converted to the same type the repository compares against. Also check that the repository delete uses a 'not equal to excludeId' filter on the session id and the user's id.
